- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent high or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.33) within 3–5 days, model overreacts to short-term volatility; apply downward bias of 1–2% per negative sentiment day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon: if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often fails to capture trend reversal; use sentiment-weighted average of recent 5-day price and sentiment to adjust forecast.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is consistently below 30-day moving average, model is biased high; apply 1–2% downward correction for next 3–5 days.
